items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: I knew Thad’s music, I knew Gil’s music, I mean that’s what I had heard

ctx.x: Wow. I like the idea of using the piano to double parts too. It definitely gives you a different tone. Not that many people employ it that way.

No it’s true. And with twelve pieces I’ve also then got support under there if I need that. I can use the piano to also help if it’s a large voicing that will help support underneath or I can have them support the trumpets or wherever it is. But I noticed that, well Brookmeyer

often had, always in his own band, had a pianist and a synthesizer. And one or the other of them, or both, were doubling different parts of the ensemble. And he got a certain sound by doing that. And Maria Schneider also often times she’ll double the upper voices of, if they’re woodwinds or the trumpets, she’ll have that covered in the piano. So her parts are a lot more notated than say Thad Jones, where it was just the harmonic information, just the chords and the pianist is left on their own kind of to figure…
